story.iWant: comprehensive tracing of all chat requests and LLM calls
story.soThat: Annie can monitor LLM performance, costs, and debug conversation flows
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Instrument `/api/chat` endpoint (AC: #1, #2) - Import tracing functions from `backend/api/observability/tracing.py` - Start trace at beginning of chat request with user_id and conversation_id - Capture request metadata: platform, message length, timestamp - Wrap request processing in try/except to capture errors - Update trace with response status on completion
- Task 2: Instrument `/api/stream` endpoint (AC: #4) - Inherit trace context from parent chat request - Create span for streaming operation - Track chunk count and streaming duration - Capture stream completion status - Handle streaming errors gracefully
- Task 3: Instrument LLM calls in `llm_client.py` (AC: #3, #5, #6) - Wrap LLM API calls with Langfuse generation tracking - Capture input prompt (truncate to 1000 chars) - Capture output completion (truncate to 1000 chars) - Extract and record token usage from LLM response - Calculate cost based on model pricing and token counts - Record model name (grok-4/chatgpt-5) and provider - Ensure fire-and-forget pattern
- Task 4: Add cost calculation utility (AC: #3) - Create cost calculation function for Grok-4 pricing - Create cost calculation function for ChatGPT-5 pricing - Document pricing source and update date
- Task 5: Testing (AC: #1-#6) - Test chat endpoint creates traces with correct metadata - Test LLM generations include all required fields - Test streaming span tracks chunks correctly - Test concurrent requests maintain isolated contexts - Test graceful degradation when Langfuse unavailable - Test cost calculations for both models

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
AC #1: Given a chat request is made to `/api/chat`, when the request is processed, then a new trace is created in Langfuse with user_id, conversation_id, and request metadata (platform, message_length)
AC #2: Given a chat request completes, when the response is returned, then the trace is updated with response status, duration, and any errors encountered
AC #3: Given an LLM call is made in `llm_client.py`, when the LLM responds, then a generation is created in Langfuse with: - Input prompt (truncated to 1000 chars) - Output completion (truncated to 1000 chars) - Token usage (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) - Model name and provider (grok-4 or chatgpt-5) - Cost calculation based on tokens and model pricing
AC #4: Given streaming is used via `/api/stream`, when chunks are streamed to the client, then a span is created capturing chunk counts, timing, and stream completion status
AC #5: Given multiple chat requests are processed concurrently, when traces are created, then each request has an isolated trace context without cross-contamination (using contextvars from Story 8.1)
AC #6: Given Langfuse is unavailable, when LLM calls are made, then the application continues without errors or blocking (fire-and-forget pattern from Story 8.1)

story-context.constraints: - Performance: Fire-and-forget tracing pattern - tracing must never block user requests (<10ms p95 overhead) - Data truncation: Prompts and completions truncated to 1000 chars per Epic requirement - Request isolation: Use contextvars from Story 8.1 to prevent cross-request trace contamination - Graceful degradation: Application continues when Langfuse unavailable (all tracing functions return None) - No breaking changes: Instrumentation is additive only - no changes to existing endpoint signatures - Cost calculation: Must accurately track token costs for Grok-4 and ChatGPT-5 with pricing from Epic 8 - Testing: Must validate concurrent request isolation to prevent trace contamination

interface.signature: start_span(name: str, metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], input: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[Any]

interface.signature: end_span(output: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], level: str) -> None

interface.name: trace_error
interface.signature: trace_error(exception: Exception, metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None

interface.name: Langfuse generation
interface.signature: trace.generation(name, input, output, model, metadata, usage, level)

tests.standards: Annie uses pytest for unit and integration testing. Tests live in backend/tests/ with separate unit/ and integration/ directories. Story 8.1 established pattern: mock Langfuse SDK with unittest.mock, test graceful degradation, validate fire-and-forget behavior. All tests must pass with Langfuse disabled (keys not configured).
tests.ideas:
**AC #1 - Chat endpoint trace creation:** - Test trace created with user_id, conversation_id, platform, message_length metadata - Verify trace ID is returned and stored in context
**AC #2 - Chat endpoint trace completion:** - Test trace updated with response status, duration on completion - Test error recording when exceptions occur
**AC #3 - LLM generation tracking:** - Test generation includes prompt (truncated 1000 chars), completion (truncated 1000 chars), token usage, model name, cost - Test cost calculation for Grok-4 and ChatGPT-5 - Verify provider name recorded (grok-4/chatgpt-5)
**AC #4 - Streaming span:** - Test span created for streaming operation - Verify chunk count and timing captured - Test stream completion status recorded
**AC #5 - Concurrent request isolation:** - Test multiple concurrent chat requests maintain isolated trace contexts - Verify no cross-contamination between traces using contextvars
**AC #6 - Graceful degradation:** - Test application continues when Langfuse unavailable - Verify no blocking when tracing fails - Test fire-and-forget pattern
